articleTitle: Semi-Supervised SAR Image Change Detection with Complex-Valued Graph Contrastive Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 8th Asia-Pacific Conference on Synthetic Aperture Radar (APSAR)
abstract: Multitemporal change detection in synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images poses a significant challenge due to severe speckle noise and limited availability of high-quality labeled samples. To address this issue, we introduce an effective semi-supervised change detection network known as Complex-valued Graph Contrastive Learning (CGCL-Net). This approach fully leverages the amplitude and phase information in SAR data, extending the change detection model to the complex-valued domain and capitalizing on SAR image advantages. Specifically, we employ an unsupervised complex-valued graph representation learning module to extract meaningful graph-level representations from complex SAR data. Additionally, a semi-supervised complex-valued graph-based change detection model is proposed for predicting change detection results with a small number of embedded labeled samples. We evaluate the performance of our method on two multitemporal SAR image datasets and compare it to other image change detection algorithms. Experimental results clearly indicate that our approach surpasses other state-of-the-art methods in SAR image change detection.

articleTitle: Land Subsidence Monitoring in Semarang (Indonesia) by SBAS-DInSAR using ALOS-2 and Sentinel-1 SAR data from 2015 to 2023
publicationTitle: 2023 8th Asia-Pacific Conference on Synthetic Aperture Radar (APSAR)
abstract: Land subsidence in Semarang is a famous environmental problem in Indonesia. This Subsidence was monitored by GPS ground surveys from 2008 to 2016 and Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) by other researchers. In this study, the SBAS-DInSAR is applied to monitor Subsidence in Semarang using ALOS-2 and Sentinel-1 SAR data. Both SAR datasets, ALOS-2 and Sentinel-1, are almost in the same observation period (2015 to 2023). This study presents the first application of SBAS-DInSAR using the ALOS-2 dataset. The updated Subsidence in Semarang City obtained by SBAS-DInSAR using ALOS-2 and Sentinel-1 is presented. The SAR dataset, ALOS-2, and Sentinel-1 show that the maximum accumulated Subsidence over eight years (from 2015 to 2023) is about 90-100 cm with an average subsidence velocity of about 11-12.5 cm/year. The subsidence area is mainly located in the north and northeast areas. The subsidence results obtained by ALOS-2 and Sentinel-1 coincide from spatial distribution and temporal transition points of view. The discrepancy between ALOS-2 and Sentinel-1 is less than 1 cm on average.

articleTitle: High-Resolution Imaging of Azimuth Frequency Scanning SAR
publicationTitle: 2023 8th Asia-Pacific Conference on Synthetic Aperture Radar (APSAR)
abstract: There is always a compromise between azimuth resolution and azimuth width for working modes using phased array to realize azimuth beam steering such as strip-map, spotlight and sliding spotlight synthetic aperture radar (SAR), which in essence redistribute the synthetic aperture time by controlling the beam direction with phase shifters. To realize high azimuth resolution and wide width imaging at the same time, intra-pulse frequency scanning technique is introduced in azimuth dimension of strip-map SAR system, which is called azimuth frequency scanning SAR. For azimuth frequency scanning SAR, there is always a beam residing in the target, and the central frequency of the beam changes with azimuth time continuously, which integrates spotlight mode and strip-map mode organically. It can not only break through the limitation of imaging area width of spotlight SAR, but also improve the azimuth resolution of strip-map SAR. Besides, the beam scanning is realized by frequency scanning array, and the antenna pattern is coupled with range frequency and azimuth angle, so as to radiate the synthetic beam to the desired direction in space without using phase shifters, which greatly reduces the hardware cost of the system. This article first introduces the principle and characteristics of beam scanning in azimuth dimension as the basis of the imaging model. And then we conduct research on signal modeling and imaging method of azimuth frequency scanning SAR to achieve high azimuth resolution. Numerical simulations verify the effectiveness of signal modeling and imaging method of the working mode, as well as the good performance in achieving high azimuth resolution.

articleTitle: Terahertz SAR Vibration Compensation Based on Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers
publicationTitle: 2023 8th Asia-Pacific Conference on Synthetic Aperture Radar (APSAR)
abstract: Due to the high-frequency and short wavelength of the terahertz wave, airborne terahertz SAR (THz-SAR) can achieve high imaging resolution, but it is sensitive to high-frequency vibration of the platform. In order to bring the image into focus, it is necessary to compensate for the high-frequency vibration error. Different from the methods that approximate the vibration as a sum of several simple harmonic vibrations, this paper proposes a high-frequency error compensation method based on alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) without modeling of the vibration, which is effective when the vibration is complex. Firstly, the coarsely focused image is obtained by the azimuth Fourier transform (FFT) to the echo signal, and the vibration compensation can be transformed into minimizing the l<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>-norm of the image. Then, auxiliary variables are introduced to construct the objective function conforming to the requirements of ADMM. In the process of iteration, an additional step is added to update the phase error by minimizing the image entropy. Finally, the estimated phase error is used for vibration compensation and imaging. The simulation results of point target and distributed imaging scene verify the effectiveness of the proposed method, and the image can be well-focused when the signal-to-noise ratio is low.

articleTitle: Circularly Polarized Lunar Regolith Simulant Antenna for Future Lunar Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 8th Asia-Pacific Conference on Synthetic Aperture Radar (APSAR)
abstract: Our work investigates a new circularly polarized antenna using lunar regolith simulant substrates. Utilizing cement, water, and lunar regolith simulant in a particular volume composition, a lunar regolith simulant substrate is fabricated. This research delivers the measurement and construction of a single CP antenna in addition to the fabrication process for a lunar regolith simulant substrate. According on measurement, the substrate referred to as lunar regolith simulant exhibits a dissipation loss (tan δ) of 0.00527 and a relatively low dielectric constant (ε<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf>) of 2.08. The circularly polarized antenna under investigation operates at a frequency of 6.175 GHz. The experimental setup utilizes two substrates arranged in a stacked configuration. Each substrate is composed of a lunar regolith simulant and has dimensions of 30 x 50 x 2 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The total thickness of two-stacked lunar regolith simulant substrates is 4 mm. A parasitic antenna is present in the top substrate's upper layer. Furthermore, the upper layer of the bottom substrate is placed by a solitary circularly polarized (CP) radiator antenna patch, while the ground plane is attached to its lower layer. The singular antenna features right-handed circular polarization (RHCP). Based on the measured results, the measured impedance bandwidth is achieved for 794 MHz, and the axial ratio bandwidth is obtained for 386 MHz. A maximum gain of 6.3 dBic can be achieved by the proposed antenna as well as, a good VSWR of 1.4 at 6.175 GHz. This work provides evidence that lunar regolith, as represented by lunar regolith simulant, exhibits significant promise as a substrate antenna for the purpose of facilitating forthcoming lunar communications infrastructure.

articleTitle: Fundamental Polarimetric Scattering Analysis For Detecting Oriented Manmade Objects Using Polarimetric Correlation Coefficients
publicationTitle: 2023 8th Asia-Pacific Conference on Synthetic Aperture Radar (APSAR)
abstract: In this research, we conduct scattering analysis for a simplified manmade objects model and investigate the polarimetric scattering characteristics, as a fundamental study for accurately detecting oriented manmade area in polarimetric SAR (PolSAR) image. The Finite-Difference Time-Domain (FDTD) method is utilized here. The model used in the analysis is made of buildings parts (four dielectric rectangular parallelepipeds) and a ground part (a circular plate), to include multiple scattering contribution between buildings in this analysis. As the ground part, three different models showing three different surface conditions are considered: 1) dielectric ground model with flat surface, 2) conductor ground model with flat surface, and 3) dielectric ground model with rough surface. Characteristics of polarimetric correlation coefficient in HV and LR bases for the models are in detail investigated for squint angle variation.

articleTitle: Sentinel-1-derived Multi-Temporal Flood Hazard of North and South Java: The Case of Bodri and Serayu Watershed
publicationTitle: 2023 8th Asia-Pacific Conference on Synthetic Aperture Radar (APSAR)
abstract: The North and South part of Java Island has their own watershed characteristic, which affects its flood dynamics. There have been many studies on flood mapping in each region but it is mostly a static model which didn’t consider the topographic or climate dynamic. Here we are developing a multi-temporal flood hazard using Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) satellite imagery Sentinel-1 collection to study the flood characteristic of each region. Each region is represented by one watershed: Bodri for the north and Serayu for the south. The result shows that areas that have high flood hazards tend to be located in densely populated areas. The reason is that flood is a compromise of high accumulation of freshwater while occasionally hazardous in certain periods. The accuracy test used in this research using TPI is limited, it is important to have a periodic flood extent map to test our result.

articleTitle: Leaf area index retrieval of oil palm plantation by Sentinel-1 satellite radar imaging
publicationTitle: 2023 8th Asia-Pacific Conference on Synthetic Aperture Radar (APSAR)
abstract: The purpose of this study is to utilize Leaf Area Index (LAI) using the radar vegetation index (RVI) based on Sentinel-1 dual-pol data VV and VH for oil palm phenological model. The study area is in oil palm plantations in PT. Perkebunan Nusantara III Sei Dadap, Asahan Regency, North Sumatra, Indonesia. The methodology is pre-processing covariance matrix, generated RVI, and correlated with oil palm phenology. The results find out the correlation between RVI and oil palm phenology, which is have quadratic model of oil palm phenology y = − 0.0004x<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> + 0.0085x + 0.3117 with R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> is 0.82.

articleTitle: Wake Detection and Ship Velocity Estimation Methods in SAR Images
publicationTitle: 2023 8th Asia-Pacific Conference on Synthetic Aperture Radar (APSAR)
abstract: The detection of wake waves in Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) images when imaging the ocean is useful for estimating the ship velocity and acquiring other ship information. However, the detection of wake waves may be difficult owing to the thinness of the wake in some images. In this study, a Gabor filter is applied by taking advantage of the features of wake waves that are most likely to be observed in ocean SAR imagery. The filter accurately extracts wake waves that extend in the same direction as that of the filter application. Furthermore, a ship velocity estimation technique is proposed that applies the information of the detected wake waves.

articleTitle: Physics-assisted Deep Learning for FMCW Radar Quantitative Imaging of Two-dimension Target
publicationTitle: 2023 8th Asia-Pacific Conference on Synthetic Aperture Radar (APSAR)
abstract: Radar imaging is crucial in remote sensing and has many applications in detection and autonomous driving. However, the received radar signal for imaging is enormous and redundant, which degrades the speed of real-time radar quantitative imaging and leads to obstacles in the downlink applications. In this paper, we propose a physics-assisted deep learning method for radar quantitative imaging with the advantage of compressed sensing (CS). Specifically, the signal model for frequency-modulated continuous-wave (FMCW) radar imaging which only uses four antennas and parts of frequency components is formulated in terms of matrices multiplication. The learned fast iterative shrinkage-thresholding algorithm with residual neural network (L-FISTA-ResNet) is proposed for solving the quantitative imaging problem. The L-FISTA is developed to ensure the basic solution and ResNet is attached to enhance the image quality. Simulation results show that our proposed method has higher reconstruction accuracy than the traditional optimization method and pure neural networks. The effectiveness and generalization performance of the proposed strategy are verified in unseen target imaging, denoising, and frequency migration tasks.

Index Terms: For Frequency Modulated Continuous Wave Radar

articleTitle: Ground Deformation in Afar Detected by ALOS-2 ScanSAR InSAR Time Series Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 8th Asia-Pacific Conference on Synthetic Aperture Radar (APSAR)
abstract: The ground deformation associated with rifting and volcanic activities in Afar has been gradually revealed by geodetic measurements such as Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) and Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) time series analysis using Sentinel-1 data. However, decorrelation of the C-band InSAR data especially in vegetated areas is still a limiting factor to obtain the spatially complete deformation signals. Recently, all ScanSAR data from L-band Advanced Land Observing Satellite-2 (ALOS-2) have been released by Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency as open and free datasets. While ALOS-2 ScanSAR InSAR may be able to detect ground deformation with high coverage, there are some challenges to overcome. For example, ALOS-2 data are strongly affected by ionospheric turbulence compared to Sentinel-1 data because of its longer wavelength. Also, ALOS-2 has a longer repeat cycle (i.e., less observation frequency) than Sentinel-1, which increases the uncertainty in velocity estimation. We carefully reduced such noise by applying methods proposed in the previous studies in ALOS-2 ScanSAR InSAR time series analysis. Consequently, both tectonic and volcanic ground deformations were successfully obtained with comparable accuracy to Sentinel-1. The derived deformation using ALOS-2 ScanSAR data has better coverage than that from Sentinel-1 data and it will enable a more detailed interpretation of the ground deformation.

articleTitle: Seasonal Variability of Internal Solitary Waves Phase Speed in the Lombok Strait Revealed by Sentinel-1 SAR
publicationTitle: 2023 8th Asia-Pacific Conference on Synthetic Aperture Radar (APSAR)
abstract: Sentinel-1 synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images have been effectively utilized to e stimate the phase speed of internal solitary waves (ISWs) in the Lombok Strait during different seasons within a year. It is assumed that ISW in the Lombok Strait generates from the interaction between the semidiurnal tides and the rough topography (sill) located in the southern region of the strait. This research employs Sentinel-1 data to calculate the phase speed of ISWs based on the detection of a single ISW packet within an image. Nevertheless, the conventional method for estimating ISW phase speed usually necessitates the detection of two packets within an image. This investigation aims to examine the capacity of SAR imagery to disclose ISW patterns and estimate the propagation phase speed within the Lombok Strait throughout different seasons. The analysis of four distinct Sentinel-1 images, each captured during different seasons, shows that the phase speed of ISWs in the Lombok Strait reaches its peak during the northwest monsoon. The differences in the phase speed of ISWs during different seasons are caused by variations in the depth of the thermocline and the presence of throughflow passing through the Lombok Strait. The results show that the ISW phase speed estimated from SAR images agrees with calculations based on the Korteweg-de Vries (KdV) equation.

articleTitle: SAR UAV for soil moisture estimation
publicationTitle: 2023 8th Asia-Pacific Conference on Synthetic Aperture Radar (APSAR)
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) equipped with Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) have revolutionized soil moisture estimation. UAV-based SAR offers high-resolution imaging, allowing detailed analysis at the field level, and greater temporal flexibility compared to satellite-based systems. The active microwave sensing capability of UAV-based SAR allows for all-weather and day-night operation, providing consistent and reliable soil moisture estimations. This paper presents a simple, lightweight, low consumption Frequency Modulated Continuous Wave (FMCW) radar attached to a hexacopter. The radar is designed to generate and acquire data in HH and VV polarization. A simple experiment is presented to estimate a soil moisture using the Dubois and the Integral Equation Model (IEM) for soil moisture detection. A custom designed convolutional network with attention mechanism for soil moisture estimation is presented.

articleTitle: Interrelationships between Satellite Imagery Pollutants and Aerosol Particles in Air Quality Assessment (NO2, SO2, O3, CO, AOD) and GNSS ZWD Data
publicationTitle: 2023 8th Asia-Pacific Conference on Synthetic Aperture Radar (APSAR)
abstract: Air pollution is a critical environmental issue with significant implications for human health and the well-being of ecosystems. In Surabaya, Indonesia, a rapidly growing urban center, the deterioration of air quality due to industrialization, urbanization, and population growth poses significant challenges. To address these challenges effectively, comprehensive air quality assessments are essential. This research focuses on utilizing satellite data, particularly Sentinel-5P, and integrating it with ground-based measurements to assess air quality in Surabaya. The study investigates the temporal and spatial patterns of key pollutants (NO2, SO2, O3, CO) and aerosol optical depth (AOD), examines their interrelationships, and explores the influence of atmospheric moisture on pollutant dispersion using GNSS Zenith Wet Delay (ZWD) data. The findings reveal insights into the dynamics of air pollution in Surabaya, providing valuable information for air quality management, policy-making, and the development of effective mitigation strategies. Furthermore, the results have potential applications in air quality forecasting and the implementation of proactive measures to safeguard public health and preserve the environment. By leveraging satellite data and cutting-edge techniques, this research contributes to a better understanding of air pollution in Surabaya and offers a foundation for evidence-based decision-making in addressing air quality challenges.

articleTitle: FASNet: Fusion Attention Siamese Network For Change Detection of Remote Sensing Images
publicationTitle: 2023 8th Asia-Pacific Conference on Synthetic Aperture Radar (APSAR)
abstract: Remote sensing change detection is an important research direction of remote sensing filed. It is the process of analyzing the differences in remote sensing images from different periods to obtain information on changes in ground targets, which is widely used in the analysis of landform and environmental changes, military reconnaissance and disaster assessment. However, change detection of remote sensing images also faces many challenges, such as light changes, seasonal changes, and noise interference, etc. In order to accurately identify the change areas of bi-temporal remote sensing images, a fusion attention Siamese network (FASNet) is proposed. FASNet adopts Siamese backbone network (ResNet-50) to obtain features from bi-temporal images. Following, pyramid dilated convolution module (PDCM) with different sizes of filters is applied to extract multi-scale context information from high-level sematic features to perceive multi-scale changes of targets. In addition, fusion attention module (FAM) is proposed to highlight the change region and suppress background interference information. Finally, a series of experiments were carried out on CCD dataset, and the experimental results prove the outperformance of our method.

articleTitle: A Novel Atmospheric Phase Correction Based on Kriging Incorporating Temporal Phase Evolution for Ground-Based SAR
publicationTitle: 2023 8th Asia-Pacific Conference on Synthetic Aperture Radar (APSAR)
abstract: In ground-based synthetic aperture radar (GB-SAR) interferometry applications, the generated interferograms often suffer from propagation delay in the troposphere, known as atmospheric phase screen (APS). Kriging interpolation is one of the approaches that can predict the APS in interferograms. In this presentation, we propose a novel Kriging approach for more accurate predictions of APS in multi-temporal GB-SAR data. In the proposed method, the temporal atmospheric phase evolution at each pixel is taken into account in the Kriging. The proposed method is validated with a real GB-SAR dataset, showing improved results on the prediction accuracy of APS in the spatial domain.

articleTitle: Application of Remote Sensing and Modelling Method in Effective Mitigating Anthropogenic Disasters due to Sea Tin Mining Activities around Bangka Belitung’s Marine Conservation Region
publicationTitle: 2023 8th Asia-Pacific Conference on Synthetic Aperture Radar (APSAR)
abstract: The Bangka Belitung Islands Province, Indonesia is one of the regions with the largest tin reserves in the world. Recently, tin mining activities shifted significantly toward the sea which threatened the environment, one of which is the sedimentation due to the tailing process. On the other hand, in 2020, Bangka Belitung Island Province allocated around 14,74% of seas region as the marine conservation area. This research will extend the previous research by using the remote sensing method to overview the Total Suspended Solid (TSS) distribution due to sea tin mining activities in the past few years and predict the TSS distribution by using the modelling method which will be focused on the Bangka Belitung’s marine conservation region. Based on the satellite imagery analysis, the radius of TSS distribution could be wider on the offshore tin mining activities than on the nearby shoreline. Furthermore, the modelling of TSS distribution shows that the offshore tin mining tailings process will cause a high distribution of TSS around the marine conservation region and could harm the food chain and reduce the productivity of the marine ecosystems.

articleTitle: Seasonal and Geographical Differences of Accuracy for SAR Sea Wind Retrieval Using Deep Neural Networks in Coastal Waters of Korea
publicationTitle: 2023 8th Asia-Pacific Conference on Synthetic Aperture Radar (APSAR)
abstract: A study was conducted to estimate sea wind in coastal waters using SAR satellite images and deep neural network (DNN) models. The Sentinel-1 SAR images from 2015 to 2020 were collected that cover the coastal waters of Korean south-east regions. Predicted wind data from meteorological forecast model results and observed wind data from sea buoys were matched-up with the SAR images to establish a training dataset for wind retrieval DNN model build-ups. Two DNN models, for eastward wind speed and northward wind speed, were created and optimized through training processes. The final results of the DNN models showed correlation coefficient (CC) of 0.901 and MAE 1.467 for eastward wind speed, CC 0.826 and MAE 1.586 for northward wind speed. The eastward wind DNN model showed a better accuracy than the northward. The difference in accuracy between the eastward wind DNN model and the northward wind DNN model was considered due to the low correlation between north wind and wave in southern sea area of Korea, especially in winter season when north wind dominates. For better accuracy, it is recommended to classify coastal regions and seasons along common marine meteorological characteristics, and to construct a deep neural network model for each classified case.

articleTitle: PSInSAR And Well Based On Land Surface Pressure and Ground Water Model In The Law of Terzaghi
publicationTitle: 2023 8th Asia-Pacific Conference on Synthetic Aperture Radar (APSAR)
abstract: Land subsidence is a global problem that increases the risk of social and economic loss. With urban development and the new need for groundwater use, concern about the recurrence of land subsidence has arisen in Japan. Land subsidence observation well (observation well) has been utilized for monitoring the subsidence, but due to the aging of facilities, remote sensing technology is attracting attention as an alternative. This paper seeks to assess the substitutability of Persistent Scatterer Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (PSInSAR) with the land subsidence observation well. For this purpose, we applied PSInSAR, Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS), and observation well to show the spatial and temporal details of land subsidence in the study area. Also, we assessed the relationship between land surface pressure and groundwater change based on the law of Terzaghi. The results revealed that the RMSE of PSInSAR and GNSS data was about 0.48 cm/year and the velocity deviation was about 0.1 cm/year. Also, the mean RMSE of PSInSAR and observation well data was about 0.13 cm, and the velocity deviation was about 1.50 cm/year. These data showed a good agreement. In the future, the PSInSAR could be the method of alternative observation wells.

articleTitle: Extraction of damaged urban areas due to the 2023 Kahramanmaraş, Turkey, earthquake using ALOS-2 images
publicationTitle: 2023 8th Asia-Pacific Conference on Synthetic Aperture Radar (APSAR)
abstract: A series of earthquakes struck Turkey and Syria on February 6, 2023. It caused serious damage in the cities and towns in the East Anatolian fault zone. In response to the request from the Turkish Government, Sentinel Asia launched an emergency response event on the same day. In this study, we extracted possible damaged areas using pre- and post-event ALOS-2 PALSAR-2 intensity images under the emergency observation. Urban footprint data were introduced because seasonal changes were significant in non-urban areas. The combination of the difference and correlation coefficient of the intensity from HH-polarization was calculated to identify changed areas. The results were verified by comparing with high-resolution optical satellite images.

articleTitle: An Improved Track-Before-Detect Algorithm for GNSS-Based Bistatic Radar Target Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 8th Asia-Pacific Conference on Synthetic Aperture Radar (APSAR)
abstract: This paper studies the global navigation satellite system (GNSS) based passive bistatic radar (PBR) object detection. Passive detection using GNSS as an illuminator has many unique advantages, such as covert operations, global coverage and low power consumption. However, the low ground power density of GNSS signals is an important factor limiting its development. Therefore, long-time energy accumulation is required to improve the signal-to-noise ratio of the target. However, long-term integration is affected by Range Migration (RM) and Doppler Spread (DS) due to target motion. In this paper, we propose a new Moving Target Detect (MTD) algorithm based on the detection of weak targets, which propose an improved Dynamic Programming-Tracking Before Detection (DP-TBD) algorithm by processing the results of the pulse-segmented Radon-Fourier transform (SRFT). This algorithm is named SRFT-DP-TBD. The algorithm is named SRFT-DP-TBD, which realizes the detection and tracking of high maneuvering moving targets with low SNR. SRFT-DP-TBD processes the echo pulse in multiple segments, jointly searches for distance and velocity and accumulates them with intra-segment, then analyzes the intra-segment signal output results and performs phase compensation during inter-segment TBD to achieve coherent accumulation. In this way, intra-segment and inter-segment coherent accumulation is realized, which significantly improves the signal-to-noise ratio of the echo signal. Finally, an experiment using GPS L5 signal as an illumination source is carried out, and a moving car is successfully detected and the track of the car is obtained by the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: A Moving Target Imaging Method for Maritime Scenarios with Azimuth Multi-Channel SAR Based on Image Quality Optimization
publicationTitle: 2023 8th Asia-Pacific Conference on Synthetic Aperture Radar (APSAR)
abstract: Azimuth multi-channel synthetic aperture radar (SAR) system can achieve high-resolution and wide-swath (HRWS) imaging simultaneously. However, moving targets in maritime scenarios suffer from ghost targets in SAR images due to channel phase errors induced by target velocity. This paper presents a novel moving target imaging method for multi-channel SAR, in which channel phase errors caused by radial velocity are estimated via optimizing image sharpness. Ghost targets are suppressed by compensating channel phase errors in image domain, during which the radial velocity of the target can also be obtained. Experimental results on simulated data verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Modified frequency domain backprojection autofocus: Experimental assessment using millimeter wave radar
publicationTitle: 2023 8th Asia-Pacific Conference on Synthetic Aperture Radar (APSAR)
abstract: Recently, drone-borne synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imaging has attracted increasing attention owing to miniaturization of millimeter wave (MMW) radars. Most studies have attempted to reconstruct SAR images of the ground observed from the sky in a simplified manner. Some of these have applied autofocus techniques to reconstruct SAR images in limited geometrical conditions. In this study, a modified frequency domain backprojection autofocus (FDBP-AF) technique is developed to generate well-focused SAR images without any geometrical limitation. The modified FDBP-AF method is precisely formulated. Its validity is confirmed by experiments in which a MMW radar is operated in a near-field radar geometry.

articleTitle: Sentinel-1 SAR Imaging for Detection and Analysis of Oil Spills in the Coastal Waters of Bintan: A Case Study and Environmental Monitoring Application
publicationTitle: 2023 8th Asia-Pacific Conference on Synthetic Aperture Radar (APSAR)
abstract: Marine oil pollution is a significant issue that can harm the ecosystem and threaten marine life. Early detection of oil spills is crucial for effective response and mitigation. In this regard, satellite technology offers a promising solution, particularly satellites equipped with radar sensors. One such satellite that can be utilized is the Sentinel-1 Radar Satellite, which can detect oil spills in marine environments. This study used Sentinel-1 Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imagery to detect and assess oil spills in the coastal waters of Bintan, Indonesia. The high-resolution VV polarization data of Sentinel1 SAR enables the identification of surface roughness, making it suitable for distinguishing oil slicks on the ocean surface. Spectral comparison and a 1.7 to 2 dB threshold were applied to discriminate the oil spill objects. Wind speed estimation from the SAR images enhanced the accuracy of oil spill detection, with wind speeds ranging from 3 to 6 m/s proving suitable for discrimination. The results emphasize the necessity for ongoing surveillance and efficient management techniques to lessen the environmental effects of oil spills in Bintan’s coastal areas.

articleTitle: Land Subsidence Observation in Bali Dense Population Area using L-Band SAR Images from 2007 to 2021
publicationTitle: 2023 8th Asia-Pacific Conference on Synthetic Aperture Radar (APSAR)
abstract: A major geological issue in the environment, especially in urban areas, is land subsidence. Monitoring and observation are crucial because they help to reduce damage to the environment, loss of human life, and the economy. We are discovering a strong, positive link between land subsidence and dense population density by utilizing the Differential Interferometry Synthetic Aperture Radar (DInSAR) method together with Pearson correlation. The Lombok earthquake may have caused land subsidence in Bali in 2018 and 2019. However, this study must be enhanced to get the main cause of land subsidence with GPS validation, correlate the rate of expansion of the region throughout each observation period, conduct continuous observations, and use longer observation periods. Last, but not least, it is still difficult to reliably get data on groundwater extraction and level.

articleTitle: Sentinel-1 Based Land Deformation Mapping in Bali Island Indonesia Using Persistent Scatterer Interferometry SAR
publicationTitle: 2023 8th Asia-Pacific Conference on Synthetic Aperture Radar (APSAR)
abstract: Land deformation is one of the key issues faced by rapidly expanding cities around the world. Land deformation can cause significant damage to the economy, infrastructure, and human life if not addressed by monitoring on a regular basis. In this research, land deformation is estimated and mapped using Persistent Scatterer Interferometric SAR (PSInSAR) in Bali Island, Indonesia. The time series Sentinel-1 dataset during 2018-2022 was acquired from the Alaska Satellite Facility (ASF) with a total of 151 images in ascending and 137 images of descending tracks. The acquired datasets were exploited using the PSInSAR technique to estimate the deformation in the study site. The maximum estimated land deformation rate in Bali Island is up to -22 mm/year which is distributed in the southern and northern parts of Bali Island over urban areas. Also, the active mountains in Bali Island are found to be unstable with a deformation rate ranging from -6 to -22 mm/year. Natural and human-induced activities such as volcanic activities, historical deductive earthquake events, active seismic faults, and active urban and infrastructure developments, could be potential factors that triggered land deformation in this study area. However, a detailed investigation and additional reference data are required to validate the results.

articleTitle: Scattering Power Components from Dual-Pol SLC and GRD SAR Data
publicationTitle: 2023 8th Asia-Pacific Conference on Synthetic Aperture Radar (APSAR)
abstract: Methods to extract scattering power components and their importance for land cover applications have been extensively studied in radar polarimetry. Motivated by the advancements, this study introduces a novel method to obtain the scattering power components from the dual-pol SLC and GRD SAR data. The idea is conceived from the two proposed indices: DpRBI and DpRSI, that characterize scattering from the built-up (i.e., "dihedral-like") and "surface-like" targets, respectively. These two indices are suitably exploited to obtain the weights for the convex splitting of the total scattered power employing the scattering power factorization framework. The proposed method is applied to dual-pol Sentinel-1 SLC and GRD data acquired over Barcelona, Spain, and Milan, Italy.

articleTitle: Scattering Analysis of Polarimetric Inverse SAR Image using Scale Model under Vegetation Canopy
publicationTitle: 2023 8th Asia-Pacific Conference on Synthetic Aperture Radar (APSAR)
abstract: Radar scattering of the hidden object under the canopy of vegetation or soil is difficult to verify without priori information of the target. A scale model of the manmade structure is deployed and measured to verify the phenomenon of the scatterer and the effect of the vegetation canopy. Full polarization inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) imaging is captured using C-band for each model. A two-dimensional polarimetric image is decomposed and its independent scattering is analyzed. It is shown that the C-band wavelength can penetrate vegetation canopy. While it is difficult to distinguish using visual images, it is shown that vegetation canopy contributes to reducing total received power by 2.7 dB. The experiment result of ISAR on scale model shows that it is coherent with the phenomenon of scattering and is a potential method to validate real SAR targets.

articleTitle: A Novel Coherence Estimation Method for InSAR
publicationTitle: 2023 8th Asia-Pacific Conference on Synthetic Aperture Radar (APSAR)
abstract: The coherence between Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) single-look complex(SLC) images, as an indicator of the similarity of Interferometric pair and the quality of Interferometric phase, has been widely applied for exploratory activities. However, coherence estimation always results in unsatisfactory accuracy due to non-ideal factors, such as nonstationary signals and estimation bias. A novel coherence estimation method is proposed to improve its accuracy for interferometric SAR (InSAR). The proposed method is modified from three aspects: the selection of statistical homogeneous points based on the coherence matrix, compensation for the interferometric phase based on a nonlinear phase model, and bias mitigation based on a mean filter. Results of both simulated and real data demonstrate that in comparison with the existing methods, the proposed method achieves higher reliability and clearer spatial features in the coherence maps, especially for complex scenes.

articleTitle: SAR Target Recognition Based on Decoupling and Reconstruction Learning Using Complex-Valued Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 8th Asia-Pacific Conference on Synthetic Aperture Radar (APSAR)
abstract: Recent years, the deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) based SAR target recognition methods are springing up. However, existing CNN-based SAR target recognition methods are limited by down-sampling caused information loss and feature redundancy, leading to learn shallow data correlations and bringing the performance collapse in practical applications of SAR target recognition. In this paper, a complex-valued decoupling and reconstruction learning (DRL-Net) based method is proposed to improve the SAR target recognition performance. DRL-Net learns the decoupling representation from the complex-valued images to make sure the learned latent feature is sparse and informative. The learned latent feature is then fed to reconstruction learning to keep the information completeness. Finally, the discriminative information is powered into the latent features to gain the semantic for SAR target recognition. Compared with baseline method, DRL-Net gains higher accuracy and faster convergence with the same number of samples. Additionally, DRL-Net exhibits a good potential for SAR target recognition with limited samples.

articleTitle: Drone-Borne InSAR using Off-the-Shelf MIMO-FMCW Radar and its Validation
publicationTitle: 2023 8th Asia-Pacific Conference on Synthetic Aperture Radar (APSAR)
abstract: Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) has been mainly mounted on satellites and airplanes. Nowadays, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), which have lower operational cost than satellites, have become as payloads of SAR. Not only developing a tailor-made radar system but some preceding researches have reported a development of drone-borne SAR with off-the-shelf components such as a vehicle-mount radar and a commercially available quadcopter. However, these drone-borne SARs still have difficulty in performing interferometric analysis due to, for example, their unreliable flight path. In this paper, we propose a drone-borne MIMO-FMCW radar-based SAR system to perform interferometric analyses. By applying MIMO-SAR principle, we can make multiple interferometric pairs with single flight and be able to make a digital surface model. If we observe multiple times, we can perform four-pass InSAR, which can detect the ground deformation from the change of topographic height. In order to obtain accurate topographic fringes, in this paper, we propose to calibrate the attitude of the radar system from corner reflectors which height is known. We report the preliminary experimental results using corner reflectors and vehicles which showed the effectiveness of the proposed strategy.

articleTitle: SAR onboard Broadband C-band Circularly Polarized Antenna for In situ Volcanic Lava Observation
publicationTitle: 2023 8th Asia-Pacific Conference on Synthetic Aperture Radar (APSAR)
abstract: Estimating the volcanic eruption scale is important for mitigating eruption hazards. While the eruption scale can be explained by the eruption mode and its temporal variation, the dominant factor is expected to be the formation reaction of volcanic products, but there are still many unknowns, including the relationship with the thermal history. To solve this problem, we proposed a broadband circularly polarized microwave antenna for a synthetic aperture radar (SAR) sensor that is suitable for in situ observation of volcanic materials such as lava. As a result of fabricating the proposed antenna, the antenna characteristics were almost the same as the simulation one, with a center frequency of 5.394 GHz, IBW=32.6%, ARBW=23.7%, and Gain=12.0dBic. The measurement results indicate that the proposed antenna has loss and radiation characteristics suitable for the purpose.

articleTitle: A Fast Near-Field 3D Imaging Method for Single-Frequency MIMO Arc Array Radar
publicationTitle: 2023 8th Asia-Pacific Conference on Synthetic Aperture Radar (APSAR)
abstract: Multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) arc array radar is a novel radar, which can obtain higher azimuth resolution and richer multi-angle information of targets with fewer array elements. However, the imaging efficiency of traditional wideband MIMO arc array radar is limited by the large amount of echo data. Single-frequency MIMO arc array radar has less echo data and the potential for efficient imaging, but the existing imaging algorithms cannot meet the requirements of practical applications. In this paper, we propose a fast 3D imaging method for near-field targets based on single-frequency MIMO arc array radar. After performing geometry-conversion compensation and matched filtering on the echo signal, the proposed method projects the echo spectrum into the image space, to reconstruct the 3D image of near-field targets. The advantages of the proposed method are low computational complexity and high imaging efficiency. Numerical simulation verifies the imaging performance of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Utilization of NTSB Report and Himawari 8 for Aviation Turbulence on Asia
publicationTitle: 2023 8th Asia-Pacific Conference on Synthetic Aperture Radar (APSAR)
abstract: One source of information on aviation accidents and aviation turbulence comes from the NTSB report. However, this report is only used for the country itself. The purpose of this study was to identify the distribution of aviation turbulence in Asia from the NTSB report and Himawari 8. Temporal distribution, spatial distribution, and Spatial Temperature Difference (STD) analysis were used in this study. Based on reports from the NTSB there were a total of 24 aviation turbulence events from 2011-2020. Most of the turbulence occurs above the ground, in the descending phase, dominantly impacting aircraft with wide bodies and minor injuries. Whereas using the Himawari 8 weather satellite, from the turbulence events where 13 satellite data are available, 5 events (38%) occur outside the clouds, and based on the STD value, countries in the tropics have higher STD values than subtropical regions both in the scene of the incident or outside the location of the incident.

articleTitle: SAR Stacking Interferometry to Monitor Critical Infrastructures and Detect Deformation Anomalies
publicationTitle: 2023 8th Asia-Pacific Conference on Synthetic Aperture Radar (APSAR)
abstract: Monitoring of critical infrastructure is crucial to continuously verify structural health and safety not only of the structures but of the surrounding areas as well. In the last decades, the use of SAR data and multi-temporal interferometric techniques proved their capability of integrating in-situ monitoring system providing deformation behavior of the infrastructures with sensitivity to small displacements, up to a few mm/year. In this work we present several case studies where dams and tailing dams have been analyzed through SAR interferometric techniques, specifically with the Small Baseline Subset approach, highlighting the importance of identifying anomalies in the temporal or spatial evolution of deformation to possible prevent catastrophic events.

articleTitle: Emergency Inundation Analysis of the August 2021 Japan Floods Using SAR Intensity Images
publicationTitle: 2023 8th Asia-Pacific Conference on Synthetic Aperture Radar (APSAR)
abstract: A heavy rainfall hit Western Japan from August 11 to 21, 2021, resulting in extensive damages caused by inundations in 68 rivers. This study utilizes two sets of pre- and post-event SAR satellite imagery to extract the inundations around Rokkaku River, a national class-A river located in Saga Prefecture, Kyushu Region, Japan. Inundation maps for August 14 at 13:13 and August 15 at 18:21, 2021 were generated using the respective satellite pairs by the different methods. These maps were validated by comparing them with aerial photos taken on August 15 and the estimated inundation data provide by the Geospatial Information Authority of Japan.

articleTitle: The Oil Quality Detection on the Gearbox of Monopulse Surveillance Secondary Radar
publicationTitle: 2023 8th Asia-Pacific Conference on Synthetic Aperture Radar (APSAR)
abstract: Accuracy and validity of surveillance data especially from Radar equipment are important to the safety and effectiveness of air navigation services, one important thing in radar systems is Azimuth Change Pulse (ACP). The motivation of this study is to explore the cause of trouble in the radar system due to the leakage of oil at the pedestal, in the gearbox antenna. The quality of oil at the gearbox influences radar performance, however, there is a leak in the system to monitor the quality of the oil. This study aims to develop oil quality detection of the gearbox by using Arduino uno, the method by prototyping method, and experimental design, the results show that the prototype runs well, and experimenting with oil from the gearbox decreases their viscosity, which reduces the quality of oil.

articleTitle: Fusion of ALOS-2/PALSAR-2 and Sentinel-1 Polarimetric Imagery with Explainable Neural Network-based Confidence Level Estimation for Glacier Surface Classification
publicationTitle: 2023 8th Asia-Pacific Conference on Synthetic Aperture Radar (APSAR)
abstract: Glacier monitoring and classification play a vital role in understanding the impact of climate change. Remote sensing imagery, particularly synthetic aperture radar (SAR) data, offers valuable information for glacier surface classification due to its all-weather and day-and-night imaging capability. This paper proposes an approach that combines dual-pol ALOS-2/PALSAR-2 and dual-pol Sentinel-1 polarimetric SAR imagery using the inverse-mapping explainable neural network for glacier surface classification. The findings indicate improved training and validation accuracies for the combination of the two SAR datasets as compared to their individual training and validation accuracies. This paper also presents a method for determining the confidence levels of the neural network in its own results. The generated confidence maps have the potential to provide valuable insights into the decision-making process of the neural network and can assist in the selection of suitable training inputs for improving the performance of the network.

articleTitle: Sea Surface Height Spatial Models of Radar Altimetry for Oceanographic Phenomena Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 8th Asia-Pacific Conference on Synthetic Aperture Radar (APSAR)
abstract: The paper especially focused on data compilations, processing, and the use of the sea-surface-height (SSH) to study oceanographic phenomena. SSH data was collected with permission from NOAA Ocean Watch data base. The numeric ASCII data was processed spatially using Er-Mapper geostatistical kriging method. Some potential application of it had been explored to reveal the phenomena of ITF Halmahera – Sorong, IOD at Indian ocean and Bali - Lombok - Timor straits, the phenomena of El Nino and La Nina, tide anomaly and tidal bore. The oceanographic phenomena in the Pacific Ocean such equatorial currents, Kuroshio and Oyashio. The possible application for coastal risk and hazards such as Tsunami wave, tidal flood, storm-surge for small islands and atolls.

articleTitle: Development and Application of Pseudo-SAR Image Simulator
publicationTitle: 2023 8th Asia-Pacific Conference on Synthetic Aperture Radar (APSAR)
abstract: In recent years, Japan has experienced a lot of accidental heavy rains inducing landslides. To reduce damage from landslides, it is necessary to take appropriate countermeasures through constant monitoring of ground deformation. Among various methods for monitoring ground deformation, SAR is superior in that it can observe a wide area with high accuracy. However, SAR image analysis is not always appropriate for some geomorphological conditions. In this study, we have developed a simulator capable of generating phase components in SAR images with arbitrary topography and ground deformation and show the usefulness of the simulator. It is confirmed that the simulated SAR images, generated based on the basic equation of phase variation caused by reflections from features, can be applied to existing ground deformation estimation methods in the same way as authentic SAR images. We also simulated some cases in which the topography and ground deformation were rotated relative to the satellite orbit. The experiments found that the characteristics and range of the ground deformation, which can be predicted from the line-of-sight (LOS) deformation estimated by PSInSAR, differed depending on the relationship between the satellite orbit and the direction of the movement.

articleTitle: The Use of MODIS and Sentinel-1 Data Fusion to Estimate Precipitable Water Vapor Values
publicationTitle: 2023 8th Asia-Pacific Conference on Synthetic Aperture Radar (APSAR)
abstract: Precipitable Water Vapor (PWV) describes the amount of water vapor in the atmosphere that potentially becomes rain. Along with the development of the space geodetic technique, water vapor can be observed using the remote sensing technology. This research uses an integration of active and optical remote sensing data which are Sentinel-1 and MODIS. Since interferogram generated by Sentinel-1 SAR images contains tropospheric delay, it can be substracted as Short Wavelength Delay (SWD) which a part of PWV value. Furthermore, the absolute PWV value is obtained by extracting parameters from MODIS atmosphere level-2. MODIS provides PWV values for reconstructing the Elevation Dependent Delay (EDD) and Long Wavelength Delay (LWD) components. We used 118 epochs to represent the rainy and dry seasons between March 2017–February 2021. The result shows that a maximum absolute PWV value of 68 mm occurred on 22/2/2020 which belongs to the time of rainy season. The estimation recorded a minimum PWV value of 20 mm on 7/6/2017 and 14/6/2018. June is when Indonesia usually experiences a dry season. Generally, the maximum and minimum daily average absolute PWV values are 68.6845 mm and 1.5884 mm, respectively.

articleTitle: Analysis of Sentinel 1 and Sentinel 2 Image for Monitoring Heterogeneous Pepper Plantation in Magelang Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2023 8th Asia-Pacific Conference on Synthetic Aperture Radar (APSAR)
abstract: Pepper (Capsicum spp) is an essential spice in Indonesia, and monitoring its supply is important for food security. The heterogeneity of pepper plantations among local farmers is a challenging problem for estimating the pepper supply. Satellite-based monitoring has been proposed to assist the local government with supplemental data to cope with pepper supply estimation. Sentinel 1 Dual Pole Radar Vegetation Index (DpRVI) and Sentinel 2 Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) were analyzed for three months on the Magelang pepper plantation. The index is correlated with the campaign data in 11 heterogeneous fields. The result shows that 63% of NDVI value has a high correlation but with a limited amount of observable satellite data. However, the DpRVI correlation yields a 72% of moderate correlation with ground observation.

articleTitle: Development of Onboard SAR Processor Using COTS GPU
publicationTitle: 2023 8th Asia-Pacific Conference on Synthetic Aperture Radar (APSAR)
abstract: Recent advances in synthetic aperture radar satellite performance has increased the volume of data on orbit and the time taken to transmit the data to the ground. As a result, the demand to shorten the time from data acquisition to delivery to the customer is increasing. To satisfy these demands, we are developing an onboard processing unit for on orbit image processing, information extraction processing using artificial intelligence and coherent change detection processing, which are conventionally performed on the ground. The feature of our developed onboard processing unit is the use of commercial graphics processing unit as a processing device. This paper describes operation examples and the development status of the onboard processing unit.

articleTitle: Design of DDS Chirp Generator using FPGA
publicationTitle: 2023 8th Asia-Pacific Conference on Synthetic Aperture Radar (APSAR)
abstract: Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) is a remote sensing technology using microwaves. Microwaves have a longer wavelength than the size of particles in the atmosphere and are not affected by clouds and fog, making it possible to observe regardless of weather conditions and sunlight. In addition, high-resolution images can be obtained by virtually synthesizing antennas.In this imaging system, the pulse compression technique is used to improve the resolution in the range direction, i.e., the direction perpendicular to the direction of motion. The pulse compression technique emits a frequency-modulated signal called a chirp signal and generates an image based on the correlation between the reflected received signal and the transmitted signal.In this paper, we present an algorithm for generating the chirp signal using a phase accumulator called direct digital. A logic circuit has been created using Quartus Prime, and simulation results are presented.

articleTitle: Interferometric phase restoration using biquaternion neural networks in PolInSAR
publicationTitle: 2023 8th Asia-Pacific Conference on Synthetic Aperture Radar (APSAR)
abstract: Singular points (SPs) in interferometric synthetic aperture radar (InSAR) data hinder the generation of accurate digital elevation models (DEMs). Since one of the main causes of SPs is polarization-and-phase distortion due to scattering, it is necessary to process polarimetric information and phase information consistently to reduce SPs. This paper proposes an interferometric phase restoration method using biquaternion neural networks (BQNNs). The dynamics of BQNNs enable processing polarimetric information and phase information as a single entity. Therefore, it can restore interferometric phase information by utilizing pixel-by-pixel polarimetric information effectively. Experimental results show that, in a certain area, a DEM generated from a BQNN-filtered interferogram is more accurate than that generated from an interferogram filtered by our previously proposed method.

articleTitle: The Evaluation of The Relationship between Land Subsidence and Building Weights in Jakarta using DInSAR
publicationTitle: 2023 8th Asia-Pacific Conference on Synthetic Aperture Radar (APSAR)
abstract: Subsidence in Jakarta is a serious problem and has a significant impact on the living environment and socioeconomy. The main causes of land subsidence are the use of underground resources and groundwater pumping. However, recent studies suggest that urban structure and building weight may also be involved. In this study, using SAR images with the DInSAR method, which can observe ground displacement and changes with high accuracy, we analyzed land subsidence in Jakarta from 2008 to 2011 and evaluated the relationship between the subsidence and urban buildings. The analysis results indicate that land subsidence is more pronounced in areas with dense-height buildings than in surrounding areas. In addition, the amount of land subsidence was not significantly affected by soil distribution in height-building dense areas, suggesting that the weight of the height-buildings affects land subsidence. Further analysis will be conducted using long-term monitoring.

articleTitle: Multi-Static Synthetic Aperture Radar for Earth Monitoring: Challenges, Innovative Solutions, and Demonstrations Using Swarms of Drones
publicationTitle: 2023 8th Asia-Pacific Conference on Synthetic Aperture Radar (APSAR)
abstract: Spaceborne synthetic aperture radar (SAR) is an essential tool for Earth observation applications. By combining multiple SAR images taken from different viewing angles, precise digital elevation models and high-resolution tomograms can be created, revealing the three-dimensional structure of vegetation, ice, and dry soil. Currently, such images are typically acquired sequentially, impacting product quality and limiting our ability to monitor rapid changes effectively. Multi-static SAR systems bring new possibilities by enabling the simultaneous collection of all necessary data, promising more effective and robust planetary monitoring. However, a significant challenge lies in developing multi-static concepts capable of generating high-quality digital elevation models and tomograms from sets of noisy and undersampled radar data acquired by clusters of smallsats with compact antenna apertures. To address this, swarms of drones equipped with radars and localization systems offer an affordable option for testing multi-static concepts and acquiring data with sub-hour temporal resolution

articleTitle: SAR Tomography Reconstruction using ISTA and GLRT Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 8th Asia-Pacific Conference on Synthetic Aperture Radar (APSAR)
abstract: SAR Tomography (TomoSAR) leverages the utilization of multiple baselines to gather data about an area, enabling the acquisition of information not only in the range-azimuth direction but also in the elevation direction. This additional information in the elevation direction primarily consists of point scatterers, with one or more scatterers typically present within a single resolution cell. This research paper examines two distinct methodologies for detecting multiple scatterers in TomoSAR: the conventional Generalized Likelihood Ratio Test (GLRT) technique and a compressive sensing (CS) approach known as the Iterative Soft-Thresholding Algorithm (ISTA). The results are examined for a simulated case of two scatterers and a real case using the TerraSAR-X dataset.

articleTitle: Exploring Diverse Polarimetric Information Contents from SAR Data
publicationTitle: 2023 8th Asia-Pacific Conference on Synthetic Aperture Radar (APSAR)
abstract: This paper evaluates three target descriptors derived from full-polarimetric SAR data. A 2 × 1 real positive target vector is defined for coherent targets based on the mean and standard deviation of complex eigenvalues of the 2 × 2 Sinclair matrix. This vector is the basis for a novel scattering-type parameter that effectively distinguishes canonical targets. In the case of incoherent targets, the scattering purity and complexity parameters are characterized using the mean and standard deviation of real positive eigenvalues from a Hermitian positive semi-definite 3 × 3 coherency (covariance) matrix. The paper demonstrates the effectiveness of these parameters through experimental analysis involving a mixture of canonical targets and further evaluates their performance using Radarsat-2 full-polarimetric SAR data.

articleTitle: Performance Verification of Scattering Power Decomposition for PolSAR Data by Using Random-rotated Dihedral Scattering Component
publicationTitle: 2023 8th Asia-Pacific Conference on Synthetic Aperture Radar (APSAR)
abstract: In polarimetric SAR (PolSAR) data analysis, model-based scattering power decomposition method is one of the most popular techniques to extract target features from the PolSAR image. Using the decomposition, the measured PolSAR data can be decomposed into several fundamental scattering models (ex. surface, double bounce, volume, helix scattering components). This technique has a problem that the volume scattering power, which is generally dominant component in vegetation/forest area, becomes dominant even in oriented urban areas where buildings are not aligned parallel to the observation orbit (oriented urban areas). Although various improved methods have been proposed to resolve this problem, no notable improvement is still not seen. In this study, we propose a novel six-component decomposition method by adding two new fundamental components. One of the new components is to express the scattering from a randomly oriented dihedral corner reflector in the oriented urban area. The another component is a dipole combined component. This represents the components that have not been formulated in the decomposition procedure using the measured covariance matrix. It is verified by PolSAR image analysis for both Pi-SAR-2X (X band) and ALOS2 (L band) data that the proposed decomposition is more effective than the previous works to observe the oriented urban area for both frequency bands.

articleTitle: Distributed-array radar system with synchronization using known targets
publicationTitle: 2023 8th Asia-Pacific Conference on Synthetic Aperture Radar (APSAR)
abstract: Recently, radar systems with distributed-array antennas, in which multiple phased arrays are distributed and the received signals from each phased array (hereafter called subarrays) are combined, have been considered to improve radar detection performance and reduce costs. However, when synchronizing the transmit–receive timing between subarrays, signal lines across boards and housings are required for synchronization, which increases the size of the equipment. To solve this problem, this paper proposes a distributed radar system in which each subarray has an independent reference signal source and uses a known signal for synchronization. A prototype of the distributed radar system is also presented, and the principle of the proposed system is verified using actual data.

articleTitle: Reconstruction of the SAR Image for a Tree Using the W-Band SAR System
publicationTitle: 2023 8th Asia-Pacific Conference on Synthetic Aperture Radar (APSAR)
abstract: The advantages of 77GHz-FMCW (Frequency Modulation Continuous Wave) RADAR, including its compact antenna size and short wavelength, have led to an increase in research demand. In particular, W-band SAR (Synthetic Aperture RADAR) utilizing 77GHz-FMCW has been applied in various fields, such as the automotive industry. However, challenges remain in the reconstruction of SAR image for a tree and the construction of the W-band SAR system. This study introduces a method for the construction of a stable W-band SAR system and a technique for the reconstruction of a SAR image of a tree. In order to construct the stable W-band SAR system, a 5-meter linear rail with the 77GHz-FMCW RADAR was accurately synchronized. In order to reconstruct the SAR image of the tree, a novel geometry and an environment of the experiment were used. A LiDAR depth map was used for precise calculation of the distance between the RADAR and the target. Coordinates of the LiDAR and the RADAR were matched, by using the corner reflector as a reference point. The quality of the constructed SAR system was evaluated using SAR image quality assessment parameters such as 3-dB resolution, PSLR (Peak Side Lobe Ratio), and ISLR (Integrated Side Lobe Ratio). By using the geometry and the environment of the constructed W-band SAR system, the SAR image of the tree was reconstructed. We compared the SAR image reconstructed by our proposed method with that obtained from the conventional method, using similarity metrics such as SSIM (Structured Similarity Index Measure) and FSIM (Feature Similarity Index Measure) for assessment. These results demonstrate the feasibility and verification of utilizing the constructed W-band SAR system and the reconstruction of the SAR image of the tree.

articleTitle: A Two-Step Target Decomposition Method for Polarimetric SAR based on Reflection Symmetry
publicationTitle: 2023 8th Asia-Pacific Conference on Synthetic Aperture Radar (APSAR)
abstract: Symmetry is an important characteristic for PolSAR data. Studying the reflection symmetry of the target is conducive to simplify the study of its scattering problem. Therefore, this paper proposes a two-stage target decomposition model based on symmetry. On the first step of the decomposition process, we decompose the coherency matrix into reflection symmetric scattering component and asymmetric scattering component. During the second step of the decomposition process, the reflection symmetric scattering component is further decomposed into surface, double-bounce and volume scattering. The asymmetric scattering component is further decomposed into helix, oriented dipole, compound dipole, mixed-dipole scattering and a new scattering which we called mixed asymmetric scattering. By extracting the non-reflection symmetric scattering component, the proposed target decomposition model could be applied without the limitation of the reflection symmetry condition. The ESAR experimental data in Oberpfaffenhofen, Germany is implemented in the paper and the results improve the defect of rough scattering characteristics analysis in the traditional target decomposition methods.

articleTitle: SAR Few-Shot Recognition based on Inner-Loop Update Optimization of Meta-Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 8th Asia-Pacific Conference on Synthetic Aperture Radar (APSAR)
abstract: At present, due to the limitations of the imaging environment and observation conditions, the automatic target recognition of synthetic aperture radar (SAR-ATR) encounters a severe shortage of target samples, which leads to poor recognition and unstable performance for few-shot targets. To address the above issues, this paper proposes an inner-loop parameter update method based on meta-adaptive hyper-parameter learning, called Mada-SGD, to achieve the goal of efficient recognition of few-shot SAR targets. In Mada-SGD, an adaptive hyper-parameter update strategy is introduced to automatically learn the initialization, weight factor, update factor and update direction in the meta-learner, it effectively solves the problem of parameter update in the meta-learning model and improves the fast adaptation of few-sample SAR targets. In addition, Mada-SGD learns the weight distribution information of initialization parameters by fully considering the correlation information between multi-step updates, which is similar to a memory mechanism and improves the feature extraction and representation ability of few-shot SAR targets. The experimental results on the customized MSTAR dataset show that the proposed Mada-SGD is able to achieve the state-of-the-art few-shot SAR target recognition performance, which verifies its effectiveness and reliability.

articleTitle: An Accelerated SBR-MOM Method for Scattering Analysis of Complex Large Targets
publicationTitle: 2023 8th Asia-Pacific Conference on Synthetic Aperture Radar (APSAR)
abstract: In this paper, shooting and bouncing ray (SBR) and the method of moments (MoM) are combined to calculate the scattering field of complex large targets. The MoM is used to calculate the edge region, while the remaining region is calculated by the SBR. At the same time, the ray tracing process is accelerated by a linear bounding volume Hierarchies (LBVH) structure and a parallel algorithm based on graphics processing unit (GPU).The effectiveness of the accelerated SBR-MoM technique is confirmed through a comparative analysis of the simulation outcomes with those obtained using the accelerated SBR approach and FEKO (RL-GO).Comparied with the accelerated SBR method, the accelerated SBR-MoM method can improve the calculation result to some extent. The comparison of the running time of these three methods shows that the efficiency of accelerated SBR-MoM is improved. It is shown that the accelerated SBR-MoM can effectively calculate the scattering field of complex targets.

articleTitle: Change Detection Analysis using Information Theoretic Measures on SAR Images
publicationTitle: 2023 8th Asia-Pacific Conference on Synthetic Aperture Radar (APSAR)
abstract: We discuss the use of two statistics for change detection in the context of Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imagery. We show their application to a bi-temporal pair of HH and VV channel intensity images from RADARSAT-2 of an agricultural scene in Winnipeg, Manitoba, Canada. The images were acquired on 7th and 31st July 2012. One of the statistics is based on a stochastic distance viz., Hellinger distance, while the other is based on the Shannon entropy which provides a measure of randomness. We have assumed the Gamma model for the HH and VV channel intensity data with mean and number of looks as the two free parameters. Test statistics are often used to design hypothesis tests after theoretically deriving their asymptotic distributions. Such hypothesis tests, to have practical utility, require a judicious choice of sample size, and a level of significance for thresholding respectively. Instead of relying on the validity of the asymptotic distribution of test statistics (i.e. an implicit assumption for using p-values and levels of significance), in this work we use the test statistics as direct quantifiers of change. We apply a simple k-means clustering with k = 2 to these quantifiers in order to segregate change and no-change regions. With these, we show that the both information theoretic measures provide substantive evidence for change detection. The corresponding change maps are studied together to understand the complementary nature of the selected statistics. It is inferred that these two statistics may be used in tandem for better change detection analysis in SAR imagery.

articleTitle: Slope Displacement Monitoring with Corner Reflectors by PSInSAR Analysis Using Sentinel-1 SAR Data
publicationTitle: 2023 8th Asia-Pacific Conference on Synthetic Aperture Radar (APSAR)
abstract: Permanent scattering points can be measured with high accuracy and are rarely obtained by PSInSAR analysis on slopes with few artificial structures, such as mountainous areas. Installing a corner reflector at the target point makes that point a permanent scattering point and enables highly accurate measurements. In this paper, the measurement accuracy of the PSInSAR analysis of the corner reflector installation position is verified by installing a corner reflector that can be forced to displace and comparing the displacement of the PS point with the actual displacement from PSInSAR analysis using Sentinel-1 SAR data. Small and cost-effective corner reflectors were installed for the slope with slight as of about 1 mm/month to confirm that displacement could be measured at the PS points of the corner reflectors in addition to the PS points of the artificial structures.

articleTitle: Investigating the Complex Signal Kurtosis for SAR Ship Classification
publicationTitle: 2023 8th Asia-Pacific Conference on Synthetic Aperture Radar (APSAR)
abstract: This paper explores the application of the complex signal kurtosis (CSK) for ship classification in single-channel synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images. Preliminary results based on the OpenSARShip dataset reveal varying trends among oil tankers, bulk carriers, container ships and fishing vessels. In addition, high-resolution samples from Capella Space were used to examine the contribution of different ship sections, which showed that the deckhouse has the strongest influence on the CSK in the majority of cases. Nonetheless, it is important to note that limitations in either the spatial resolution or the number of available samples restrict the generalisability of the results. Consequently, this paper emphasises the necessity for a large, open dataset consisting of complex-valued, high-resolution samples to comprehensively investigate the role of the CSK, as well as phase information in general, for ship classification.

articleTitle: Assessing Three-Dimensional Displacement in the Low Latitude Area from Multi-Geometry Sentinel-1 InSAR: Case Study Palu City
publicationTitle: 2023 8th Asia-Pacific Conference on Synthetic Aperture Radar (APSAR)
abstract: Interferometry Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) technology has revolutionized displacement monitoring. Still, accurately discerning the North-South component in low-latitude regions is a challenge. This research investigates the significance of horizontal movement for accurate 3D displacements in Indonesia, with Palu City as a focus. Utilizing a time-series 3D decomposition with the Least Square Adjustment method, findings reveal urban areas experiencing vertical land subsidence, and uplift in active hill regions, with predominant northward horizontal displacement. Comparison with GNSS measurements demonstrates the accuracy of the 3D displacement model. This study underscores the necessity of horizontal movement consideration in 3D displacement monitoring in low-latitude areas, offering insights for geohazard analysis, disaster readiness, and infrastructure blueprinting.

articleTitle: X-band Circularly Polarized Microstrip Array Antenna for Full Polarization UAV-SAR
publicationTitle: 2023 8th Asia-Pacific Conference on Synthetic Aperture Radar (APSAR)
abstract: In the realm of regional emergency observation and real-time, high-resolution data acquisition, there is a burgeoning interest in the development of UAV equipped with Synthetic Aperture Radar systems (UAV-SAR). However, a critical challenge lies in achieving a UAV-SAR system that meets criteria such as high resolution, lightweight design, minimized payload, power efficiency, operational viability at high altitudes, robustness in extreme environments, extended flight durations, and full polarimetric functionality.To address this challenge, our research group envisages the creation of an X-band circularly polarized UAV-SAR system, designed specifically for disaster management and environmental monitoring, leveraging the 25 kg payload capacity of the UAV platform. The effective functioning of the SAR system necessitates a broadband antenna with complete circular polarization capabilities to ensure precise observations. The antenna must also be compact, lightweight, possess high gain, accommodate broadband chirp pulse signals, and exhibit excellent antenna isolation and axial ratio (AR).To this end, we put forth a novel design featuring a 4×4 array antenna outfitted with axe-shaped radiating elements. The proposed antenna underwent rigorous simulation, fabrication, and assessment within an anechoic chamber. Additionally, an indoor polarimetric scattering SAR experiment was conducted employing canonical targets to assess the polarimetric SAR proficiency of the system equipped with the proposed antenna.

articleTitle: Characteristic Analysis of Ground Deformation in Chiba Prefecture Using Sentinel-1 Data
publicationTitle: 2023 8th Asia-Pacific Conference on Synthetic Aperture Radar (APSAR)
abstract: Ground deformation due to natural gas mining has been reported in the Chiba Prefecture. For example, in Yachimata City, the land subsided by approximately 40 cm from 1976 to 2020. In addition, reclaimed lands are found around Tokyo Bay, and periodic ground deformation monitoring is necessary. In this study, we utilized the short baseline subset (SBAS) method to determine the spatial tendency of the subsidence using Sentinel-1 to elucidate the characteristics of ground deformation in the Chiba Prefecture. The analysis was conducted using paired images of the ascending and descending orbits from January 2017 to December 2019, to determine the displacement velocity in each line-of-sight direction. Consequently, we quantitatively confirmed a large ground displacement in the Yachimata area. The estimated displacement velocity was evaluated using reference data, and the results showed that the characteristics of the variation were captured, although some residuals were observed.

articleTitle: Drone Borne SAR Tomography as a Powerful Subsurface Survey Tool
publicationTitle: 2023 8th Asia-Pacific Conference on Synthetic Aperture Radar (APSAR)
abstract: Tomography using drone-borne synthetic aperture radar (SAR) has proven to be very useful and efficient in surveying the subsurface of areas with gravimetric soil moisture ranging from 0 to 50%. The drone-borne SAR, along with the back-projection processing algorithms, and the proof of concept through the detection of a corner reflector buried 1.7 meters deep in clayey soil, are presented. Anthills with areas ranging from 0.05 m2 to 120 m2 were detected under an industrial eucalyptus forest, with a detection probability of more than 80% in two different regions.

articleTitle: A Phase Synchronization Technique for Multistatic SAR Systems Based on a Microwave Link
publicationTitle: 2023 8th Asia-Pacific Conference on Synthetic Aperture Radar (APSAR)
abstract: Phase synchronization poses a significant challenge for multistatic synthetic aperture radar (SAR) systems. A novel concept called MirrorSAR has been introduced, which relies on a configuration of transmitter and receiver satellites positioned at separate locations. In this setup, the receiver satellites serve as mirrors or space transponders, redirecting the radar echoes back to the transmitter. This arrangement simplifies the receiver functionality and enables the utilization of cost-effective platforms, particularly in the emerging NewSpace domain. Within the transmitter, the forwarded radar signals are coherently demodulated using the same oscillator responsible for generating the radar pulses.
